limitations: Normalized listings are research evidence, not runtime admission fingerprints.
No native fixtures, full transformed method or Editor executed.
Removing copies needs shared exact-definition lease, complete failure/order/geometry controls and independent native CPU/RSS comparison.
Sample counts are not calls, CPU shares or removable-time estimates.
JDK CompilerInlining events are absent in both recordings; no causal inlining claim.
Observed leaf shifts do not explain the CPU regression by themselves.
Absence of setters in h alone cannot prove coordinate immutability across exposed context points/callbacks.
Vector copy elision is only a candidate; no complete transformed method, allocation measurement or host speed claim.
